key_insight: The paper proposes a Bayesian optimization framework to track a rigidly moving 3D target’s position and orientation from far-field data across time, using analytical motion models for translations and rotations.
engineering_relevance: This enables noninvasive object tracking in wave-based sensing systems, with potential use in radar, sonar, and inverse-scattering-based monitoring.
method: Derive far-field pattern formulas for translated and rotated targets.
Model translation and rotation as independent stochastic processes over successive time steps.
Use Bayesian optimization to jointly estimate location and orientation; identify unknown shape at the initial time with a fully connected neural network trained on precomputed data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments validating the framework and a posterior consistency result for the probabilistic model.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate stochastic motion assumptions and on the quality of the precomputed dataset used for initial shape identification.
paper_title: Bayesian optimization approach for tracking a moving target from far-field data in three dimensions
